overview: 6-month, full-time (≈6 h/day) roadmap to move from fundamentals to intermediate backend engineering and system-design readiness. Months 1–3 build strong foundations (CS, programming, web APIs, databases, testing). Months 4–6 focus on deployment, cloud, architecture, security, scaling and a single multi-part capstone that ties everything together. Plan balances hands-on projects, incremental integration of tools, and professional skills for hireability.

Basic OS concepts (processes, threads), memory basics
Classes & objects, inheritance, encapsulation, SOLID basics
Basic Git commands, branching & merging workflow
Linux commands, filesystem, permissions, basic shell scripting
Python syntax, data types, control flow, functions
Arrays, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues (implementation exercises)
objectives: Understand and reason about algorithmic complexity
Write clean, object-oriented Python code
Use Git for source control and collaborate via branches

tips: Treat one day per week (e.g., Sunday) as a review & consolidation day: recap notes, fix weak spots, update flashcards and backlog.
Keep one repository that evolves each month (the capstone) so incremental work becomes a portfolio piece—commit often with clear messages.
Use time-boxed study blocks (90–120 min) with short breaks (Pomodoro variants) to maintain focus across 6-hour days.
Pair practical work with small theory sessions: after learning a concept, spend an hour implementing a tiny, test-covered example.
Prioritize depth over breadth when tired: solidly finishing core modules (APIs, DB, Docker, CI/CD, testing) yields outsized returns.
Document progress and decisions (ADRs, README); this habit both clarifies thinking and creates interview/demo material.
If you fall behind, trim lower-priority supporting topics (Node/TypeScript, GraphQL) and keep the capstone and core infra on track.
Schedule weekly mock presentations: explaining your architecture and trade-offs improves both retention and communication skills.
